 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 12.3.2020 at about 3.45 p.m. Srinivas H.M. was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-JK-6208 infront of Adigas Hotel, situated at Kanakapura main road, at that time, driver of the tractor bearing registration No.KA-42-T-1101 and trailer bearing No.KA-42-8891 coming from Konankunte cross towards Talaghattapura on Kanakapura main road, Bengaluru with rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler, the left side middle tire of the tractor passed in his belly.
Consequent to which, Srinivas H.M. sustained grievous injuries .

3. It is stated in the petition that, immediately Srinivas was shifted to Matru Hospital,
later he was shifted to Sanjaygandhi and again shifted to Victoria Hospital.
The doctors of the Victoria Hospital informed that the said Srinivas brought dead.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent huge amount towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

4. It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
and was aged about 46 years, doing field work and fixing the roofs in the petrol bunk work and earning Rs.38,000/- per month.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.

sentences.text: It is alleged in the petition that, the alleged accident was occurred, due to the negligent act of the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-42-T-1101 & KA-42-8891.
As such, the Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle, in Crime No.44/2020.
Accordingly, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
6. After registration of the case, notice was issued to the respondent.
In response to the notice, the respondent has not appeared before the court, remained absent, placed exparte.

7. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 placed her affidavit evidence,
in lieu of examination-in-chief and examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.

Since the respondent has not appeared before the court to contest the case of the petitioner,
the matter was set down for arguments.
8. Heard the argument of learned counsel for the petitioners.
And perused the materials available on record.

9. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, this court has framed the following points;
POINTS 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Srinivas H.M. had died due to injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 12.3.2020 at about 3.45 p.m., infront of Adigas Hotel, Kanakapura main road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor & trailer bearing registration No.KA- 42-T-1101 & KA-42-8891 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
4) What order or award?
10.

My answers to the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative.
Point No.2: In the Affirmative Point No.3: Partly in the Affirmative.

Point No.4: As per final order, for the following:

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-42-T-1101 &
KA-42-8891 alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Srinivasa H.M. had died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondent.
12. On the other hand, the respondent being the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle placed exparte.
In such a situation, it is necessary to go through the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion with respect to the above point.

On going through the above point,
burden is on the petitioners to prove the same on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
13. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
Ex.P1 is the true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.44/2020 of Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic Police Station.
Ex. P2
is the true copy of the first information statement given by one Muthuraju.
Ex.P3 is the true copy of the mahazar.
Ex.P4 is the true copy of the seizure mahazar.
Ex.P5 is the true copy of the sketch, Ex.P6 is the true copy of the IMV report, Ex.P7 is the inquest mahazar, Ex.P8 is the P.M. report.
Ex.P9 is the true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.44/2020 of Kumaraswamy Traffic police.

14. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Muthuraja, the S.H.O. of Kumaraswamy Traffic police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 &
304(A) of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 3(1) R/W Section 181, Section 56/192 R/w Section 146/196 of M.V. Act for not having driving licence, insurance policy and F.C.
15.
This material document remained unquestioned and unchallenged by the respondent.

The silence of the respondent in connection with the case of the petitioners make this court to draw adverse inference against him holding that, he deemed to have admitted all the allegations made against him.

The respondent neither has not made an effort to come forward to file written statement in answer to the case of the petitioners nor made an effort to adduce rebuttal evidence to shaken the case of the petitioners.
16. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above point.
Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle Tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-42-T-1101 & KA-42-8891.
In the said accident, Srinivasa H.M. had died.
Accordingly, I am answering the Point No.1 is in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: These two points are taken together for common discussion, in order to avoid the repetition of facts.

18. Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P10 to Ex.P16, Aadhar cards of the petitioners &
death certificate of the deceased and his mother, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

19. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 in being the wife,
petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children and the petitioner No.4 being the father have lost the deceased, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondents herein, have not produced documents to show the independent economic status of the petitioners.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
20. The petitioners herein, have not placed any documents to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through post mortem as per Ex.P8, the age of the deceased has been mentioned as 43 years.
In the absence of the any authenticated documents, it is apt to be considered the P.M. report that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 43 years.
For his age, multiplier '14' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

21. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing field work and fixing the roofs in the petrol bunk under one Sathish Kumar R. and was earning Rs.38,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the petitioner, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2020.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.14,500/- for the year 2020.
22 . Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the Lakshmi M vs Manjunatha M on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90362842/

sentences.text: An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

"
23. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
24.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are four persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
25. In the present case, deceased was aged about 43 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "14" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years, 25% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.14,500/- per month.
And Rs.1,74,000/- per year.

Along with this, the future prospects of 25% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,74,000+43,500) =
Rs.2,17,500/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,63,125/- (Rs.2,17,500-Rs.54,375).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "14" which comes to Rs.22,83,750/-.
26.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others
, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

27. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral Lakshmi M vs Manjunatha M on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90362842/
6 expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 4 under the head loss of consortium.

LIABILITY:
30.

In so far as, liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle accident in question had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in this regard remained unshaken.
As per the documentary evidence, the owner of the offending vehicle had no valid driving licence and valid insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
As such, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation determined by this court to the petitioner along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Accordingly, I am answering the point No.2 in the affirmative and the point No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.

Point No.4:
31.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,92,750 (Rupees twenty four lakh ninety two thousand seven hundred and fifty only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle Tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-42-T-1101 & KA-42-8891.
18. Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
The respondents herein, have not produced documents to show the independent economic status of the petitioners.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
20. The petitioners herein, have not placed any documents to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through post mortem as per Ex.P8, the age of the deceased has been mentioned as 43 years.
In the absence of the any authenticated documents, it is apt to be considered the P.M. report that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 43 years.
For his age, multiplier '14' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the petitioner, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

And Rs.1,74,000/- per year.

Rs.2,17,500/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
28. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
As such, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation determined by this court to the petitioner along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Accordingly, I am answering the point No.2 in the affirmative and the point No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/-.
